term: Use of artificial intelligence by the United States Department of Defense
definition: The United States Department of Defense has been analyzing and employing military applications of artificial intelligence since at least 2014.
details: The program initially focused on drones and other robots, but has also been using large language models for military research and analysis. The current US policy on lethal autonomous weapons is Department of Defense Directive 3000.09, updated in January 2023.

explainer.lead: The US Department of Defense has analysed and employed military AI applications since at least 2014. Its policy choices shape how autonomous and AI-enabled systems are deployed.

tiers.eli5: The US military has been studying and using AI for years, starting with robots and drones and now also large language models.
tiers.practitioner: Early work centred on drones and other robots; large language models are now used for military research and analysis. Pitfall: policy governs what is permitted — current US policy on lethal autonomous weapons is DoD Directive 3000.09, updated January 2023.
tiers.paperLevel: A government programme of military AI analysis and adoption since at least 2014, governed for lethal autonomous weapons by Department of Defense Directive 3000.09 (updated January 2023).

explainer.example: A defence research group uses large language models to analyse documents as part of military research.
